title: My Biggest Stock Gain Ever
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Joseph Carlson After Hours reports his biggest single-day portfolio gain ever: up $65,000, or 4.5%, with his portfolio back near all-time highs. His thesis is a rotation: money is leaving the 'bottleneck' AI winners — semiconductors, memory and energy suppliers such as Nvidia, ASML, Micron (down 6% on the day), SanDisk (down 8.25%) and Bloom Energy (down 7.6%) — and moving into the big-tech companies that buy those supplies and own the customer relationship. On the day Amazon rose 6.4% to $266, Microsoft 6.13%, Google 4%, Mastercard 3%, S&P Global 3.56%, Moody's nearly 5% and Netflix 4%, with ASML the only holding in the red. He then covers Duolingo's earnings: daily active users rose 29% year on year to 64.9 million, paid subscribers grew 14% to 13.1 million, and the stock jumped 32–35% to around $170, leaving his $41,000 position down only about 15%; he argues AI disruption fears were wrong. Uber's quarter gets similar praise: gross bookings up 20% on a $60 billion base, trips up 16%, demand exceeding driver supply, and a $10 billion-plus autonomous-vehicle commitment. Finally he argues the midterm results are not bearish for big tech: opposition to new data centres makes existing permitted capacity scarcer and more valuable. No explicit buy, hold or sell rating and no fair value is stated for any ticker in this video, so no call-event is recorded; his Netflix $10,000 buy plan near $60 is mentioned as almost triggered, with the stock now on watch. Auto-captions garble Duolingo as 'Dualingo' and S&P Global as 'S&B Global' in places.
